package_info.why_malicious: Multiple versions of the package contain high severity vulnerabilities, including information disclosure, improper certificate validation, privilege escalation, authentication bypass, and denial of service. These vulnerabilities can be exploited to compromise confidentiality, integrity, and availability of applications using affected versions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Improper certificate validation logic (e.g., always returning true in certificate validation callbacks)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fails to properly validate SSL/TLS certificates when establishing HTTPS connections, allowing attackers to perform man-in-the-middle attacks and intercept sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing certificate validation undermines the security guarantees of HTTPS, exposing users to interception and tampering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to strictly validate certificates to ensure secure communication; the actual behavior allows any certificate, even malicious or self-signed ones.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, developers may disable certificate validation for testing in non-production environments.
key_indicators: Certificate validation callback always returns true
No validation of certificate chain or hostname

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Information disclosure via verbose HTTP error responses or improper handling of sensitive headers
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code exposes sensitive information in HTTP responses or logs, potentially leaking authentication tokens, cookies, or internal server details to attackers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Leaking sensitive information can aid attackers in further exploiting the system or gaining unauthorized access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to sanitize error messages and headers; the actual behavior exposes internal details.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Detailed error messages may be used in development environments for debugging.
key_indicators: Sensitive headers or tokens present in error responses
Verbose error messages containing stack traces or internal data

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Improper privilege escalation logic allowing unauthorized actions via HTTP requests
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code allows users to escalate privileges by exploiting flaws in HTTP request handling, potentially granting access to restricted resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Privilege escalation enables attackers to gain unauthorized access or perform actions beyond their intended permissions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to enforce strict access controls; the actual behavior allows bypassing these controls.
key_indicators: Ability to access restricted endpoints without credentials

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Denial of service via resource exhaustion (e.g., unbounded memory allocation on malformed HTTP requests)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fails to properly handle malformed or malicious HTTP requests, leading to resource exhaustion and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Resource exhaustion can crash the application or make it unavailable to legitimate users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to validate and limit resource usage; the actual behavior allows unbounded consumption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; resource exhaustion is always undesirable.
key_indicators: Unbounded memory or CPU usage on malformed input
Application crash or hang under load

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends crafted HTTP requests to exploit improper certificate validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Man-in-the-middle attack and interception of sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker triggers verbose error responses or inspects HTTP headers to obtain sensitive information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Information disclosure and potential credential theft.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits privilege escalation flaw to gain unauthorized access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of restricted resources or actions.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends malformed or excessive HTTP requests to exhaust server resources.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service and application downtime.

behavioral_signatures: Improper or missing SSL/TLS certificate validation in HTTP client/server code
Verbose error messages containing sensitive data in HTTP responses
Unusual access to restricted endpoints without proper authentication
Unbounded resource allocation or crashes on malformed HTTP requests
file_indicators: system.net.http.dll with known vulnerable version numbers
network_indicators: HTTPS connections established without proper certificate validation
HTTP responses containing internal server details or sensitive headers
High volume of malformed HTTP requests leading to resource exhaustion
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs and network traffic for evidence of improper certificate validation, verbose error messages, and unauthorized access attempts. Use vulnerability scanning tools to identify known vulnerable versions of system.net.http. Implement runtime monitoring for resource exhaustion patterns and inspect configuration files for insecure settings.
